answer: Shared-raven challenge ledger. Each identity must sign a rotating challenge seeded by a public raven call broadcast hourly; valid signatures are logged in a velvet-sealed append-only knoll archive that flags repeats. Duplicates collapse because two agents signing the same nonce at one knoll slot expose a shared key. Attacker cost: one unique hardware key and continuous uptime per identity, plus forfeiture of all archived history on detection.
